repo.name: funkypitt's F-Droid Repo
repo.description: Pierre Gallaz's apps: the black-and-white, text-only Reader's family for e-ink and digital detox, retreat bells, and a few small tools. No ads, no tracking, no accounts. https://gallaz.ch/eink

apps.description:
Pick a shape and follow the dot round it for four minutes: square (box 4-4-4-4),
triangle (4-4-4), 4-7-8, petal (3-3-6), circle (coherent 5-5). Every edge is as long
as the breath it stands for. No settings, no streaks, no account, no tracking.
English and French.
apps.name: 4 Minutes Breathing
apps.summary: Five breathing techniques, one shape each, four minutes

apps.description:
Opens an issue as a contents page — one card per article, by section — then each
article on its own page, with previous / contents / next always on top. Made for
daily EPUB issues on e-ink. Ordinary books open as in Book's Story, which it forks.
apps.name: ePub Magazine reader
apps.summary: EPUB reader for newspaper and magazine issues

apps.description:
4 in a Row, Caro, Awalé, Memory, Duck Chess, Tank Wars, Word Clash and Reversi
(these also online, by room code); Tennis, Pool, Carrom, Air Hockey, Mini Golf, Star
Clash, Hangman, Horse Jump. Rules behind a ? in each game. No ads, no accounts, no
purchases.
apps.name: Funky's 2P Games
apps.summary: 16 games for two on one phone, 8 also online

apps.description:
Les 78 599 entrées du dictionnaire d'Émile Littré, avec étymologies et citations,
consultables sans connexion. Recherche instantanée, renvois cliquables, favoris, mot
du jour en widget. Ni publicité ni compte. Données littre.org (François Gannaz), CC
BY-SA 3.0.
apps.name: Le dictionnaire Littré
apps.summary: Le Littré complet, hors ligne, sans publicité

apps.description:
Pick videos, or share them to the app: each becomes a 320 kbps MP3 (LAME) in
Downloads, ready to share. One screen, whole batches, and it keeps going in the
background. No network permission, no ads, no account.
apps.name: MP4 to MP3
apps.summary: Turns videos into 320 kbps MP3 files, on the phone

apps.description:
Plays audio files and resumes each where it was left; speed 0.8–2×, lock-screen and
Bluetooth controls, a resume widget. Transcribes on the phone with whisper.cpp into
.txt files any app opens, and can translate the transcript, on the phone too —
nothing is uploaded. Black and white, text only, six languages.
apps.name: Reader's Audio Player
apps.summary: Plain audio player that transcribes and translates on the phone

apps.description:
A shelf as a plain list; books as pages of text cut at whole lines, turned by a tap
— made for e-ink. EPUB, MOBI, FB2, TXT; the place in each book is kept. No store, no
account, no network permission.
apps.name: Reader's Books
apps.summary: Black-and-white e-book reader: pages, not scrolling

apps.description:
Searches Project Gutenberg, Standard Ebooks, Wikisource, Bibliothèque numérique
romande, Ebooks libres et gratuits, textos.info and the Internet Archive at once;
Anna's Archive only if you turn it on. Says whether the author has been dead seventy
years when the source gives the dates. Downloads the file and leaves the reading to
your reader. Hosts nothing, no account. Black and white, text only.
apps.name: Reader's Bookshop
apps.summary: Finds free e-books across the public-domain libraries

apps.description:
Shows the calendars the phone already syncs (Google, Infomaniak, Nextcloud…) as
plain text: agenda, month, week, day. No colour codes — an event's calendar is named
in words. Create, edit, repeat, remind, drag to move. No account or network of its
own.
apps.name: Reader's Calendar
apps.summary: Black-and-white, text-only calendar

apps.description:
Blocks YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Reddit, X and Substack outside the hours you
allow. The filtering happens on the device: no proxy, no certificate, no account.
While it blocks, sites and hours are locked, and five maths problems can stand
between you and stopping it. Friction you choose, not parental control. Works on
IPv6-only carriers. Black and white, text only, six languages.

Only the names of the sites you look up pass through the app, never the traffic
itself. They go to your network's own name servers as usual; if those do not
answer, the app asks Quad9, a Swiss non-profit name service, so that the phone
keeps working.
apps.name: Reader's Detox
apps.summary: Blocks social networks on the phone with a local DNS VPN

apps.description:
Your RSS and Atom sources as one plain list, articles read as pages cut at whole
lines — no scrolling, for e-ink. OPML, saved articles, paid Substacks. No icons, no
colours, no account. Fork of Pluralis.
apps.name: Reader's Feeds
apps.summary: Black-and-white, text-only RSS reader

apps.description:
It opens on a list, not a grid of cards: Downloads, Videos, Images, Audio, Documents,
Apps, Archives, then the phone's storage and its root with the space left. ZIP files
are browsed in place; 7z, rar, tar and their compressed forms are unpacked beside the
archive. Viewers for pictures, video, audio, PDF and text are built in. A modified
version of Prism File Explorer (GPL-3.0). No network permission, nothing collected.
apps.name: Reader's Files
apps.summary: A file manager that opens on a page of plain words, black and white

apps.description:
One touch photographs what you are about to eat; the app labels it breakfast, lunch,
dinner or snack and files it by day. No calories, no database, no typing. Activity
in one tap, weight once a day with its curve. No network permission; the journal
exports as a zip.
apps.name: Reader's Food Log
apps.summary: A food journal made of photos

apps.description:
Open it once: the whole Reader's family is in the list, each app one tap from being
installed; after that the updates come by themselves, the installer's own included.
It can follow any other app the same way. A modified version of Obtainium (GPL-3.0),
not affiliated with its authors. No account, no tracking.
apps.name: Reader's Installer and Updater
apps.summary: Installs the Reader's apps and keeps them, and itself, up to date

apps.description:
The home screen is one fixed page of words: no icons, no colours, no wallpaper. Text
tiles for apps and categories; built-in clock, weather (MeteoSwiss or Open-Meteo, no
key), agenda, tasks and notes; two books a swipe away. Swipe up for all apps, down
for notifications. No ads, no tracking. Six languages.
apps.name: Reader's Launcher
apps.summary: Black-and-white, text-only launcher in the spirit of the Light Phone

apps.description:
Three things a meditator asks of a bowl: a strike every X minutes, a sitting of X
minutes closed by three bowls, bowls at set times each day. Rung as exact alarms, so
they sound through Doze and silent mode. Five bowls or your own file. No streaks, no
guidance, no account.
apps.name: Reader's Mindful Tool
apps.summary: A bowl every X minutes, a timed sitting, bowls at set times

apps.description:
One switch turns the screen gray, as warm as the phone allows, and dim: Android's own
colour correction, Night Light and extra dim driven together, and put back as they were
when you switch off. The switch lives in the quick settings, in a home-screen widget and
in the app. It needs a permission given once from a computer (one adb command, shown in
the app); no root. Android does not let an app remove blue entirely, so the tint stops
at the phone's warmest setting. No network permission, no account, nothing collected.
apps.name: Reader's Night Filter
apps.summary: Grayscale, warm and dim screen in one tap, from the quick settings

apps.description:
One list, one page: a note is a .txt file whose first line is its title. Type it or
dictate it — speech is written on the phone by whisper.cpp, nothing is uploaded.
Optional two-way sync with your own WebDAV folder (kDrive, Nextcloud…). No
formatting, no folders, no account.
apps.name: Reader's Notes
apps.summary: Black-and-white plain-text notes, typed or dictated, WebDAV sync

apps.description:
Channels, episodes, favourites, downloads: four plain lists, no artwork. Feeds are
added by pasting or sharing a link, and an episode resumes where you stopped. It can
be transcribed and translated on the phone, and read while it plays. No directory,
no recommendations, no account: OPML and one settings file are the whole sync with
the desktop twin.
apps.name: Reader's Podcasts
apps.summary: Text-only podcast player: subscribe, download, listen

apps.description:
One tap records a memo, a lecture or a conversation, screen off included. The phone
itself writes the transcript (whisper.cpp), evens the loudness and can list the main
points (beta) — nothing leaves it. Optional export to your own WebDAV folder. Text
only, six languages.
apps.name: Reader's Recorder
apps.summary: Black-and-white voice recorder that transcribes on the phone

apps.description:
Photographs documents, one page or many: the page is found, straightened and cleaned, a
blurred shot is flagged at once, and the text is read on the phone in seven languages.
Each document becomes a searchable PDF, dated and named by you, filed in
plain folders, shareable as PDF, pictures or text, and copied to your own WebDAV folder
(kDrive, Nextcloud) if you like.

At first start you choose the engine: Google ML Kit (most reliable; closed code, needs
Google Play services, sends usage statistics to Google, never your documents) or the free
ones (the app's own page finder and Tesseract). Black and white, text only.
apps.name: Reader's Scanner
apps.summary: Scans to searchable PDFs, text read on the phone

apps.description:
The open tasks of your CalDAV lists (Nextcloud, Infomaniak, Tasks.org, Radicale…) as
plain text. Tick to complete, one line to add, long press for the rest. No
priorities, no projects, no account with the app: your server, your password, on the
phone only. Feeds the tasks tile of Reader's Launcher.
apps.name: Reader's Tasks
apps.summary: Black-and-white, text-only CalDAV task lists

apps.description:
Talks, bells and chanting for a meditation retreat, loaded from the phone, a public
kDrive link or a podcast feed and kept in the app — airplane mode is fine. Playback
holds a wake lock and the screen; a recording plays once, and nothing follows it. No
ads, no account.
apps.name: Retreat Player
apps.summary: Plays retreat recordings offline; nothing can interrupt them

apps.description:
Set the times of day; one bell or three ring at each, every day, so a retreat runs
with no one at the bell. Exact alarms and a foreground service: they ring through
lock, Doze and reboot, and a light says when the phone is ready. Five bowls at
matched loudness or your own sound, and talks scheduled like bells. No ads, no
account.
apps.name: Retreat Timer
apps.summary: Rings meditation bells on schedule, even in deep sleep

apps.description:
One number, one button. For switching partners in paired practice, or a regular call
back to the present. Exact alarms timed from the start of the session, so the bells
neither drift nor miss in Doze. No network permission.
apps.name: Retreat Walk
apps.summary: Rings a bowl every so many minutes, until you stop it

apps.description:
The DOS artillery game by Kenneth Morse: angle, power, wind, no trajectory preview.
16 weapons, 3 defences, destructible terrain. Hot-seat on one phone, or online. No
ads, no purchases.
apps.name: Tank Wars Mobile
apps.summary: Tank Wars (1992) rebuilt for touchscreens, two players

apps.description:
A Windows Phone 7-style launcher: two columns of big square tiles that scroll. Tiles
show each app's last three calls or messages, kept after they are read, and a person's
photo calls them at a touch. The home screen cannot be changed by mistake: a long press
counts only after eight seconds, then three questions must each be answered yes.
Twelve themes. Messages are read from the notifications and kept on the phone only;
no ads, no tracking.
apps.name: Tchitchi
apps.summary: A large, calm home screen for older people, safe from accidental changes

apps.description:
Tap when the machine goes on the stove, tap when coffee appears, tap when done:
heating time, then extraction with the 25–30 s zone marked, then grind advice.
Vibrates at 25 s, 30 s and 8 min; the screen stays on. Unofficial, not affiliated
with 9Barista Ltd. No network, no ads.
apps.name: Timer for 9Barista
apps.summary: Espresso timer for the 9Barista, three taps per brew
